clients.name: LifeTimerCore
clients.role: Shared timer behavior, settings contract, CloudKit reconciliation, and diagnostics

clients.name: Life Timer web
clients.role: Browser timer with local fallback and private CloudKit settings sync

clients.name: Life Timer
clients.role: Native host UI, local read-only HealthKit sleep overlay, Screen Time report host, and Live Activity control

clients.name: Life Timer WidgetsExtension
clients.role: Hour Live Activity and Dynamic Island presentation

clients.name: Life Timer Watch App
clients.role: Native Watch host UI and CloudKit refresh

authorities.authority: LifeTimerCore plus progress-v1 shared parity fixture
authorities.conflictRule: Swift and JavaScript must pass the same versioned fixtures
Last writer by client timestamp wins; local App Group/browser state remains usable and pending while offline
Never synchronized unless a future versioned contract explicitly adds presentation state

authorities.authority: Owner-authorized HealthKit sleep-analysis samples on the iPhone or iPad
authorities.conflictRule: Read-only visible-range query; merged in memory by category; never synchronized, logged, or backed up by Life Timer

authorities.authority: Owner-authorized Apple Device Activity report data
consumers: Life Timer Screen Time report extension only
authorities.conflictRule: Current-device-only aggregate buckets rendered inside the sandboxed extension; host receives no activity records; local enable preference is never synchronized

environments.name: github-pages-production
environments.deployCommand: GitHub Actions .github/workflows/pages.yml after authorized push to main

commands.setup: Requires Xcode 26, Swift, Node.js, Git, and iOS/watchOS simulator SDKs

data.classification: private personal lifetime settings, transient HealthKit sleep data, and sandboxed Screen Time activity
data.authoritativeStore: Newest timestamped lifetime settings revision cached locally and mirrored through the user's private CloudKit database; HealthKit remains authoritative for sleep and Apple Device Activity remains authoritative inside the Screen Time report extension

credentials.name: CloudKit JS API token
credentials.purpose: Browser-visible selector for the Life Timer CloudKit container
credentials.location: Web/cloudkit-config.js; Allowed Origins managed in CloudKit Dashboard
credentials.scope: Public identifier restricted to https://ayaksic.github.io; private records still require Apple authentication

credentials.name: Apple signing identity and provisioning profiles
credentials.purpose: Sign native apps/extensions and authorize App Group/CloudKit capabilities
credentials.location: Apple Developer account, Keychain, and Xcode-managed profiles
credentials.scope: Life Timer bundle IDs, Family Controls host/report extension, group.yaksic.lifetimer, and iCloud.yaksic.lifetimer

releaseIdentity.versionSurface: Native diagnostics show CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion; web diagnostics show artifact version/build
releaseIdentity.commitSurface: Native generated LifeTimerBuildInfo.plist bundle resource and generated Web/build-info.js artifact
releaseIdentity.environmentSurface: Native and web diagnostics show runtime plus production CloudKit container
releaseIdentity.lastSyncSurface: Native diagnostics sheet and expandable web sync diagnostics

authentication.mechanism: Public timer; Apple CloudKit authentication is required only for private settings sync
authentication.resetRecovery: Apple account recovery; local timer remains functional without sync

authorization.model: CloudKit private database scopes records to the authenticated Apple user

encryption.keyOwner: Apple for CloudKit; Personal Data Vault owner for off-site archives

dataLifecycle.retention: Until the owner deletes local/CloudKit state or the Apple account/container

logging.retention: Apple/GitHub platform-managed; application emits no private settings payload logs
